output.overview: Lead with the next renewal, then show its price and date. One source directly supports this approach; the cancellation source addresses a nearby need but demonstrates features outside this app’s promise.
searchNotes: Analysis uses only the supplied captions, transcripts and indexed frame descriptions. No images were attached.
Only track-1 is directly relevant. cancel-1 provides adjacent context, not evidence for bank linking or cancellation features in this app.
The frames at 4s and 7s do not establish either video’s opening or whole-video compliance. Suggested hooks below are original concepts, not exact source quotes.
All proposed visuals use generic interface graphics with no logos, people, hands, body parts or photorealistic humans.

qualifications.reason: Cancellation serves the nearby need of managing unwanted subscriptions. That motivation can inform the creative, but bank linking and automatic cancellation do not transfer to the stated tracking promise.
qualifications.hook: Supplied caption: “Cancel subscriptions in one tap.”
qualifications.title: Subscription cancellation

qualifications.reason: Listing subscription prices and renewal dates directly addresses knowing what renews and when. The calendar presentation transfers naturally to the proposed phone interface.
qualifications.title: Prices and renewal dates

angles.title: What Renews Next?
angles.label: Calendar reveal
angles.description: Open with the app’s central question, then highlight the nearest upcoming renewal and its price in a generic phone calendar.
angles.whyItFits: Makes the promise immediately understandable through one concrete answer.
angles.evidence: track-1’s transcript describes listing subscription prices and renewal dates in a calendar. Its supplied 4s frame description reads “Renewal calendar.”
angles.visualDirection: Animate a standalone phone mockup against a plain background. Move an editorial highlight from today to the next renewal, then enlarge its name, date and price. Use generic text labels; no logos, humans, hands or body parts.

angles.title: Put a Date on It
angles.label: Price list to calendar
angles.description: Begin with subscription prices, then reveal the matching renewal dates and calendar positions so viewers can consider what to keep.
angles.whyItFits: Connects the price list to the timing information that makes this tracker useful, without implying that the app cancels subscriptions.
angles.evidence: track-1’s narrator says they list prices and renewal dates in a calendar “so I can decide what to keep.” This supports the decision-making premise, not a claim of savings.
angles.suggestedHook: You know the price. When does it renew?
angles.visualDirection: Use an editorial animation of generic subscription rows gaining date labels, followed by a calendar view inside a standalone phone mockup. Use typography and simple shapes only; no logos, humans, hands or body parts.

storyboard.title: What Renews Next?
storyboard.premise: A 24-second calendar demonstration answers one renewal question. All entries are clearly labeled illustrative demo data.

scenes.visual: Text question beside a standalone phone showing a generic renewal calendar. Small “Demo data” label. Plain graphics only; no logos, people or body parts.
On the same phone, an editorial highlight selects the nearest renewal: “Music plan · Nov 12 · $9.” No logos, people or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: See the next renewal, its date, and its price.

scenes.visual: Cut to a generic price list with matching renewal dates, then back to their calendar positions. Keep the demo label visible. No logos, people or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: Put your subscription prices and renewal dates in view.

scenes.visual: Calendar remains beside the text “See renewals coming” and “Check your next renewal.” Generic phone and typography only; no logos, people or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: Know what renews and when. Check your next renewal.
